FOREWORD
This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Plain Bearings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. The standard was originally published in 1981. The present revision has been necessitated to align with the international standard IS0 6525 : 1983. Requirement of thrust half washers would be covered separately in Part 2 which is under preparation. This standard covers ring type thrust washers and is in conformity with IS0 6525 : 1983 `Plain bearings - Ring type thrust washers made from strip - Dimensions and tolerances', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ).

5.2 Grooves serve the primary purpose of feeding oil over the flat areas. Some typicai grooving arrangements are illustrated in Pig. 2. 5.2.1 When grooves are embossed into bimetallic materials, the depth of groove should preferably be less than the lining thickness. 5.2.2 Sharp edges of grooves shall be removed.

Standard Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
